title: Degree of a closed point of a scheme over a field
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a field and $Y_0$ a scheme over $k_0$, with structure morphism $f:Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, and let $x\in|Y_0|$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points]. Its residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a field extension of $k_0=\kappa(f(x))$ through the homomorphism induced by $f$. The *degree* of $x$ is

$$
 \deg(x)=[\kappa(x):k_0],
$$

the dimension of $\kappa(x)$ as a $k_0$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], with the convention $\deg(x)=0$ when this dimension is infinite. When $Y_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$, the residue field of every closed point is a finite extension of $k_0$ [lem-kun-closed-point-field], so $\deg(x)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ for every $x\in|Y_0|$.

source.place: §27 (Integrality), p. 157: "Let $x$ be a closed point of $X_0$. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is a finite extension of $\mathbf F_q$; we set $\deg x=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$"; also Deligne, Weil I, (1.1), p. 274 ("Posant $\deg(x)=[k(x):\mathbf F_q]$")

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: `deg(x) = f.residueDegree x` for the structure morphism `f : Y₀ ⟶ Spec (.of k₀)`, since `(Spec (.of k₀)).residueField (f x) ≅ k₀` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.residueFieldIso` (same file, line 301: the residue field of the field `k₀` at its only prime, the zero ideal, is `k₀`), and `Module.finrank` is invariant under this isomorphism; the convention 0 for an infinite extension is Mathlib's

lean_notes: The source repository's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degreeOver` (WeilConjectures/ZetaSeries.lean:228, closed) is this definition with the identification κ(f x) = k₀ made explicit through `Hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap` (line 221): `Module.finrank k (X.residueField x)` for the algebra structure `k →+* X.residueField x` induced by `f`.
